correctness.rationale: From source AGC ratio |h x|/max(|x|,epsilon)>lambda, the small-norm threshold is |x|>lambda*epsilon/h and all three stated branches follow (continuous at a and epsilon). For 0<eta*h<2, each nonzero branch decreases |x| strictly; a nonzero positive asymptotic magnitude is excluded by continuity and strict decrease. For eta in [2/h,2/lambda], both proposed phases lie in the closed [a,epsilon] interpolation where gradient equals lambda*epsilon*sign(x), so x->x-s->x; endpoint a and epsilon agree with adjacent formulas. For eta>2/lambda the outer factor |1-eta*lambda|>1 is invariant for sufficiently large |x| and diverges. Independently used exact fractions h=5,lambda=1,epsilon=1/10,eta=1/2: a=1/50, s=1/20, x=1/40 gives x->-1/40->x. The infinity statement is universal convergence, not convergence of all intermediate trajectories to cycles.
residual_risks: Scalar deterministic plain GD only; no stochastic, momentum, vector, or full network inference.

value.rationale: The positive AGC parameter norm floor is an implemented safeguard for zero/near-zero weights; the sharp h rather than lambda stability ceiling and exact cycle band reveal a mathematical limitation of the very safeguard. This is a motivated source-specific discrete dynamical boundary rather than renaming a textbook scalar GD threshold.
residual_risks: Interpretation is limited to one scalar deterministic unit, not empirical neural-network instability.

final_claim: For a scalar h-curvature quadratic and AGC parameter-lambda clipping with floor epsilon>0 (h>lambda>0), the exact three-zone clipped gradient has boundaries a=lambda*epsilon/h and epsilon. Every initialization converges to zero iff 0<eta*h<2. For 2/h<=eta<=2/lambda, nonzero two-cycles have positive phase x in [max(a,eta*lambda*epsilon-epsilon),min(epsilon,eta*lambda*epsilon-a)]; for eta>2/lambda some trajectories diverge. Formally setting epsilon=0 gives stability iff eta*lambda<2.
limitations: Formal zero-floor comparison is not the actual AGC default
No higher-dimensional or noisy SGD conclusion
No assertion that all intermediate nonconvergent trajectories tend to the displayed cycles.
